rules.localIntel: Hand-curated from primary sources: each item was read at its own source on the date shown, states only what that source says, and quotes it where a quote is given. Where a source does not settle something (a winner, an end date) the item says not verified. Every link is re-checked on each daily build; an item whose source has gone is withdrawn until it is re-sourced. This is not a census: it lists the contracts, formularies and papers found and read, not every one that exists.
rules.frameworks: NO NHS SUPPLY CHAIN FRAMEWORK IS COUNTED HERE, AND THAT IS THE FINDING RATHER THAN A GAP. On 12 September 2026 the Hub's record covered all 140 contract launch briefs NHS Supply Chain published - 121 parsed framework names, 16 unparsed and 3 expired - and all three lists were searched: not one name is mental health, and NHS Supply Chain runs no mental health category. ONE AGREEMENT TOUCHES THIS PATCH AND IT IS NAMED HERE RATHER THAN COUNTED: Medical Healthcare Furniture, reference 2024/S 000-025534, category Facilities and Office Solutions, starting 12 May 2025 and ending 11 May 2027 with an option to extend a further 24 months, 13 lots and 51 suppliers. Two of its lots are this patch and both are quoted from NHS Supply Chain's own contract launch brief: Lot 3 Challenging Environment Furniture and Lot 5 Multi-sensory. WHY IT IS NOT COUNTED: NHS Supply Chain publishes supplier names per agreement and never per lot, so claiming it would put all 51 furniture suppliers - hospital trolleys, birthing furniture, recycling bins, portering chairs, workstations on wheels - in front of a rep as the mental health market. The reference is given so a rep can go straight to the right agreement and the right lot. Every date, reference, lot name and count in this paragraph was read on NHS Supply Chain's own brief on 12 September 2026. COVERAGE LIMIT, STATED RATHER THAN HIDDEN. This patch is three markets that share a name. The MEDICINES, which are the largest identifiable spend on it, are bought by pharmacy against the Drug Tariff on a prescription, not by mental health, and they appear in no framework and no Part IX line here; they belong to the Hub's Pharmacy and Medicines page. The SERVICES - talking therapies, crisis provision, CAMHS beds, autism and ADHD assessment, learning disability services - are commissioned by integrated care boards, councils and mental health trusts, which is why almost every buyer in the awards list below is one of those three and why almost none of it is a product buy. The only part of this patch a product rep sells into directly is the ESTATE AND WARD ENVIRONMENT: anti-ligature fittings, challenging-environment furniture, doors and vision panels, seclusion and de-escalation spaces, staff safety systems and sensory rooms. That market has no national framework, no published market-share data and no product catalogue, and is bought through capital projects and a trust's own estates team. The ligature, challenging-environment and refurbishment rows in the awards list are the visible edge of it and are the rows to start from.
rules.suppliers: NO SUPPLIER LIST IS PUBLISHED FOR THIS SPECIALITY, because this panel names suppliers only where a framework record names them on this speciality's own frameworks, and this patch has none. The 51 suppliers on Medical Healthcare Furniture are not reproduced here: that list is published per agreement rather than per lot, so it would name the furniture market rather than the challenging-environment market inside it. THE SUPPLIER ANSWER ON THIS PATCH IS NOT A FRAMEWORK AND NOT A CATALOGUE. There is no national agreement, no published market-share data and no product catalogue for the ward environment; it is bought through capital projects and a trust's own estates team. The awards list below names the providers that actually won work on this patch, which is weaker evidence than a framework supplier list and is labelled as such. rules.awards: Award-stage notices whose TITLE matches /\b(mental health|mental illness|camhs|psychiatr\w*|psycholog\w*|psychother\w*|talking therap\w*|iapt|counselling|eating disorder\w*|autis\w*|adhd|learning disabilit\w*|neurodevelopmental|neurodivers\w*|ligature|seclusion|challenging environment|restraint training|suicide|self[- ]?harm|electroconvulsive|recovery college|forensic\w*|crisis (?:text|house|alternatives|resolution|team|line))\b/i and does not match /\b(education(?:al)? psycholog\w*|psychology services group|forensic (?:vacuum|science)|dna profiling|forensic property|forensic consumables|pay as you go forensic|glass washers|environmental audit\w*)\b/i. The exclusion list exists because every pattern in it matched a real notice that was not this speciality, and there were eight: four educational psychology contracts bought by local authority education directorates (Rutland twice, West Northamptonshire, Milton Keynes), the Ministry of Justice's HMPPS Psychology Services Group court and parole reports service, two police forensics buys - a forensic vacuum metal deposition chamber and DNA profiling kits - and an estates/accessibility audit (Neurodiverse Environmental Audits, Oxford Health NHS Foundation Trust) matched on 'neurodiverse'. Prison healthcare is deliberately NOT excluded: HMP Wandsworth counselling, bought by Oxleas NHS Foundation Trust, and Northern Ireland Prison Service challenging environment furniture are both this market and both stand. A CPV code beginning 85111500 or 85121270 is recorded as corroboration where the feed carries one, but never admits a notice on its own: a notice carrying a basket of CPV codes is filed under all of them and bought under one. Buyer names are never matched on.
rules.openTenders: Notices still open for bidding, matched the same way. An empty list means no open notice on this patch today, not that none was looked for.
rules.drugTariff: No Drug Tariff part applies to this speciality. Part IX reimburses dressings and elastic hosiery (IXA), incontinence appliances (IXB), stoma appliances (IXC) and elastic hosiery (IXR); nothing on this patch is listed there, so the panel carries no tariff rather than reaching for the nearest part.
rules.directorySuppliers: No supplier directory label maps to this speciality, so no directory-tagged supplier is listed. That is a gap in the directory's vocabulary, not a finding that no company sells here, and no neighbouring page's list is borrowed to fill it.
rules.gpPrescribing: Items prescribed in primary care in England (GP practices and other prescribers NHSBSA attributes to a practice) and dispensed in the community, aggregated to ICB. Not hospital in-patient use, and not the trust-level hospital prescribing dataset. Source: NHSBSA Open Data: English Prescribing Dataset (EPD) with SNOMED code. Each market below is a set of BNF codes exactly as NHSBSA classifies them, named with the market. Figures are for the latest month in the dataset (202609) with a 12-month total; a change on the same month a year earlier is published only where that month had at least 25 items, and otherwise no percentage is printed. Share is share of ITEMS by NHSBSA product (BNF code characters 1 to 11, split to 13 where a catch-all code holds several brands). It is product share, not company share: the dataset does not name the company, and one company can hold several products. An ICB's leaders are ranked within that ICB's own total for the same market and month. Contains public sector information licensed under the Open Government Licence v3.0. Source: NHS Business Services Authority.
rules.mhraDsu: Every MHRA Drug Safety Update that GOV.UK itself tags to a therapeutic area mapped to this speciality in config/mhra-dsu-speciality-map.json. The speciality comes only from GOV.UK's own facet, never from the title or the text. The monthly 'Letters and medicine recalls sent to healthcare professionals' roundup is left out (15 here), and so is any update GOV.UK ticks against 30 or more therapeutic areas, which is a message to everyone rather than to this speciality (2 here). Newest first; the count is every tagged update in the archive, and the list shows the most recent. MHRA Drug Safety Update, GOV.UK, as at 2026-11-25.
rules.drugTariffViiia: NHSBSA Drug Tariff Part VIIIA, the basic prices of generic medicines, for effective month 2026-11: narrowed to the lines whose medicine NHSBSA prescribes under BNF 04.01 or 04.02 or 04.03 or 04.04. The BNF code is the one NHSBSA attaches to the line's VMP SNOMED code in its English Prescribing Dataset, the same classification-first approach as the Part IX slice, never a medicine-name pattern. 56 of the 3,532 lines in the file carry no BNF code because the medicine was not prescribed in primary care in the months read, so this slice can understate the range and does not overstate it. Every count and price is taken from the lines selected. Prices are the basic price at publication, converted from the pence NHSBSA publishes, and are not necessarily today's. The list shows at most 80 lines, Category M first.

localIntel.org: NHS Dorset (Dorset Formulary)
localIntel.title: Dorset Formulary 04.02.02 Antipsychotic depot injections
localIntel.date: No date printed on the page
localIntel.fact: Flupentixol decanoate, haloperidol decanoate and zuclopenthixol decanoate are listed as Formulary. Aripiprazole injection is Formulary for maintenance in adults with schizophrenia who responded to oral aripiprazole but are non-compliant. Olanzapine embonate (ZypAdhera) and paliperidone prolonged-release suspension (Xeplion) are Formulary, hospital use only. Risperidone LAI (Risperdal Consta) is listed with no new patients to be initiated, and the entry points to paliperidone LAI. Paliperidone 3-monthly (Trevicta) is for patients stable on paliperidone LAI for at least 6 months, and new requests need approval from the Dorset Healthcare Medicines Management Team. The page prints no review date; supplier names are not on the page.
localIntel.quote: New requests for Trevicta must be approved by Dorset Healthcare Medicines Management Team
localIntel.use: Paliperidone is the steer here: Xeplion is hospital-initiated and Trevicta needs a named local team's approval, so a long-acting injectable case in Dorset goes through that team, not through primary care.

localIntel.org: NHS Dorset (Dorset Formulary)
localIntel.title: Dorset Formulary 04.04 Methylphenidate, modified-release brand tiers
localIntel.date: No date printed on the page; the page links a system guidance document dated Jan 26
localIntel.fact: Methylphenidate is Formulary for use per NICE NG87 and the local shared care protocol, children and adults. For modified-release tablets, Affenid XL and Xaggitin XL are first line and Xenidate XL and Matoride XL are second line; prescribers should specify the preparation name. Concerta is non-formulary due to high cost, and all formulary MR tablet preparations are described as bioequivalent to Concerta. The linked guidance document itself was not read: not verified.
localIntel.quote: Xaggitin and Affenid are best value / first choice brands
localIntel.use: A named first-line pair and a non-formulary originator brand. A modified-release methylphenidate brand outside Affenid XL and Xaggitin XL starts in Dorset as second line or off formulary.

localIntel.org: Nottingham and Nottinghamshire ICB (Notts APC)
localIntel.title: ADHD medications shortages: post-supply recovery guidance, V1.0
localIntel.fact: Prescribing of 12-hour prolonged-release methylphenidate tablets returns to brand prescribing after the shortage, with no blanket switching. For new patients the specialist names the brand at shared-care initiation. The preferred brands for modified-release tablets are Atenza XL, Affenid XL, Delmosart and Xaggitin XL (spelled as the guidance prints them). 8-hour capsules (Equasym XL, Focusim XL, Medikinet XL, Meflynate XL, Ritalin XL and others) must always be prescribed by brand and not switched in primary care. Guanfacine is RED, specialist-only. The Preferred Prescribing List itself was not read: not verified.
localIntel.quote: In Nottinghamshire, the preferred brands for methylphenidate modified release tablet prescribing are Atenza XL®, Affenid XL, Delmosart® and Xaggitin XL® (bioequivalent to Concerta® XL).
localIntel.use: A dated list of four preferred brands with a review date of May 2027. Any brand not on it is moved to a preferred brand at routine review or when the GP is comfortable to switch.

localIntel.org: Leicester, Leicestershire and Rutland (LLR formulary)
localIntel.title: LLR Formulary 04.01.01 Hypnotics
localIntel.date: No date printed on the page
localIntel.fact: Zopiclone is First Choice and zolpidem Second Choice, to be considered if the patient has a hangover effect with zopiclone. Temazepam is Restricted, for patients who cannot tolerate other choices or who have previously responded to it. Promethazine is Formulary for short-term use, and the entry says NICE does not recommend sedating antihistamines for insomnia. Inpatient recommendations: PRN hypnotics at most 5 nights out of 7, none before 11pm, and regular prescriptions given a 2-week review date. Prescriptions are to follow NICE NG215 on dependence-forming medicines. Supplier names are not on the page.
localIntel.quote: All regular hypnotic prescriptions should be assigned a review date of 2 weeks to ensure usage does not become long-term
localIntel.use: A dependence-forming class held to a short-course, first-choice-only position, with CBT for insomnia as the stated next step. Anything beyond zopiclone first and zolpidem second needs a case against that wording.

localIntel.org: Leicester, Leicestershire and Rutland (LLR formulary)
localIntel.title: LLR Formulary 04.01.01 Melatonin: brand-specific entries
localIntel.date: No date printed on the page
localIntel.fact: Melatonin is Restricted. For children and adolescents aged 6 to 17 with ADHD, Adaflex is first line and Ceyesto 1mg/ml oral solution is named by brand, with patients on other liquid brands or prescribed generically to be switched to it. Colonis melatonin 1mg/ml solution is flagged as contraindicated in children because of its excipients. Modified-release: generic MR melatonin is to be prescribed, Slenyto is first line for ages 2 to 18 with autism spectrum disorder or Smith-Magenis syndrome and second line for ADHD ages 6 to 17, and Circadin is not supported for primary insomnia over 55. The page names brands only, not suppliers: not verified.
localIntel.quote: To prevent the dispensing of a product that is not suitable for paediatrics, Ceyesto should be prescribed by brand.
localIntel.use: One of the few formulary entries that names a melatonin liquid by brand and rules out another by name. The yellow classification applies only up to 10mg daily, per the page.

localIntel.org: Northamptonshire Healthcare NHS Foundation Trust
localIntel.title: Northamptonshire Healthcare NHS FT Rehabilitation Services, six independent-sector providers on Direct Award C
localIntel.fact: Six award notices from the Trust, all titled Rehabilitation Services, name six providers under the Provider Selection Regime Direct Award C: St Andrews Healthcare (GBP 204,930), St Matthews Healthcare (GBP 3,908,970), Elysium Healthcare Limited (GBP 156,862), Cygnet Behavioural Health Ltd (GBP 2,132,942), Cygnet (D/H) Limited (GBP 516,450) and Pottergate Centre (GBP 64,680). That is GBP 6,984,834 across the six notice values. Each contract is dated 01/04/2025. The notices describe the provider as an existing one reviewed through a Key Criteria assessment and the contract as not changed considerably from the previous one. Term, end date and extensions are not verified, and the notices do not say whether the value is annual or total.
localIntel.quote: has not changed considerably when compared with the existing/previous contract delivered by the named provider
localIntel.use: Rehabilitation placements for this Trust sit with a fixed set of independent providers, two of them Cygnet entities, and were rolled over rather than re-tendered. A supplier selling into locked or specialist rehabilitation wards would be dealing with those providers, not the Trust. The notice values are not verified as annual.

localIntel.org: Hertfordshire Partnership University NHS Foundation Trust
localIntel.title: HPFT Mental Health Rehabilitation Services, awarded to Turning Point (Services) Ltd
localIntel.ends: Award notice: 04/10/2029, extendable to 04/10/2032 (1+1+1); contract notice 104334-2026 gives 15/06/2029, extendable to 15/09/2032
localIntel.fact: Turning Point (Services) Ltd is the named supplier on the award for the Trust's social care mental health rehabilitation pathway (Intensive Enablement Service, Midpoint in Stevenage and The Stewarts in Harpenden), run as an open procedure. The award notice (059843-2026, published 25/06/2026) shows GBP 7,182,207.67 with a contract period 05/10/2026 to 04/10/2029 and a maximum extent to 04/10/2032. The later contract notice (104334-2026, published 03/11/2026) shows a contract signed 11/09/2026 for GBP 3,382,805.54 with a period 14/09/2026 to 15/06/2029 and a maximum extent to 15/09/2032. The two sets of dates and values are not reconciled here, so the term is not verified beyond the range they give.
localIntel.quote: The Service is a social care mental health rehabilitation pathway, which is aimed at supporting Service Users into semi-independent or independent living and return to live and participate in community activities.
localIntel.use: A third-sector provider, not an NHS unit, holds this block-contracted rehabilitation pathway in Hertfordshire until at least mid-2029, so equipment or digital outcome-tracking offers go to Turning Point. The notice says the Service will adopt a recovery outcome measure tool agreed with the Trust.

localIntel.org: Coventry and Warwickshire Partnership NHS Trust
localIntel.title: Specialised Residential Care (Mental Health) and Rehabilitation Service, Hawkesbury Lodge, awarded to Rethink Mental Illness
localIntel.fact: Rethink Mental Illness is the named supplier on the award for a 14-bed mental health residential and rehabilitation unit at Hawkesbury Lodge, Coventry, bought by a competitive flexible procedure with supplier dialogue. The award notice (096923-2026, published 14/10/2026) shows a value of GBP 3,000,000 net (GBP 3,600,000 gross), a contract period 27/10/2026 to 30/09/2029 and a maximum extent to 30/09/2031 with a 24-month renewal. The award status in the record is pending and a signature date of 26/10/2026 is scheduled; whether it was signed is not verified.
localIntel.quote: a newly refurbished 14 bed unit in Coventry, West Midlands, for the accommodation of suitable patients currently placed out of area.
localIntel.use: The unit exists to bring out-of-area patients home, so it is a repatriation route: the buying decision on fit-out, equipment and digital tools in the unit sits with Rethink, not the Trust. Whether Rethink holds any supplier framework for that is not verified.

localIntel.org: North Staffordshire Combined Healthcare NHS Trust
localIntel.title: North Staffordshire Combined Healthcare NHS Trust out of area PICU placements, six direct awards to Cygnet and Priory units
localIntel.fact: Six award notices under the Provider Selection Regime (the four August 2026 notices state Direct Award Process B; the two October 2026 notices are confirmation notices that give no process letter in the text read) place named patients in out-of-area psychiatric intensive care beds: Cygnet Sherwood (GBP 28,980, signed 13/07/2026), Priory Hospital (GBP 28,616, signed 16/07/2026), Cygnet Hospital (GBP 28,980, signed 29/07/2026), Cygnet Hospital (GBP 28,980, signed 03/08/2026), Cygnet Godden Green (GBP 30,268, signed 19/09/2026) and Cygnet Appletree Back (GBP 30,268, signed 01/10/2026). Each is for a single patient, the notices state that all known providers were contacted and only one responded in time, and no term is stated. The six are spot placements, not a framework.
localIntel.quote: This is highly specialised psychiatric services with limited availability nationally.
localIntel.use: The Trust has no contracted PICU provider for these patients and buys by the bed per patient, mostly from Cygnet sites. That is the out-of-area demand signal: capacity is the constraint, not price. Individual notice values are not annual contract values.

localIntel.use: Greater Manchester's own PICU capacity is shut and has been replaced by independent-sector beds under one named supplier, so PICU-related equipment and safety products are being bought for Priory sites rather than the Trust's estate while that lasts. localIntel.org: NHS Somerset Integrated Care Board
localIntel.title: Digital Mental Health and Emotional Wellbeing Service for Children and Young People
localIntel.ends: 5 years from 01/04/2027 plus an optional extension of up to 2 years (tender stage, no award)
localIntel.fact: A competitive tender for a Prime Provider of a digitally enabled emotional wellbeing and mental health service for children and young people. The record states a GBP 750,000 envelope for the five years excluding VAT and a maximum of GBP 1,050,000 over seven years. The tender period closed 09/09/2026. The procurement is run by NHS South, Central and West on behalf of the commissioners, ahead of an ICB merger effective 01/04/2027. No supplier is named and no award is recorded. Any DTAC or clinical safety requirement in the tender documents is not verified.
localIntel.quote: The new service will commence on the 1st April 2027.
localIntel.use: A digital children's mental health service in Somerset is open to a prime provider with a start date of April 2027, so the awarded supplier is not yet known. Check the notice for an award before approaching.

localIntel.kind: Supply contract award (below threshold, no competition)
localIntel.org: Homerton University Hospital NHS Foundation Trust
localIntel.title: C&H Talking Therapies PCMIS system licence, PCMIS Health Technologies Ltd
localIntel.fact: PCMIS Health Technologies Ltd is the named supplier on a below-threshold award made without competition, value GBP 18,340 excluding VAT (GBP 22,008 gross), signed 05/08/2026, running 01/10/2026 to 31/03/2027. The record describes the scope as the PCMIS licence with maintenance, support, hosting, SMS appointment reminders and online e-referral. Which services use it beyond City and Hackney Talking Therapies is not verified.
localIntel.quote: Provision of PCMIS system licence providing maintenance, support, hosting, sms patient appointment reminders, online e-referral
localIntel.use: City and Hackney Talking Therapies run their patient record and e-referral on PCMIS, a six-month licence due to end 31/03/2027, so a replacement or add-on digital tool would come up for decision around then. Renewal intent is not verified.

localIntel.org: NHS Supply Chain
localIntel.title: Medical Healthcare Furniture, 13 lots and 51 suppliers, Lot 3 Challenging Environment Furniture and Lot 5 Multi-sensory
localIntel.ends: 11/05/2027 (option to extend for an additional 24 months)
localIntel.fact: NHS Supply Chain's contract launch brief for Medical Healthcare Furniture, reference 2024/S 000-025534, gives a start of 12 May 2025, a run of 24 months and an end of 11 May 2027, with an option to extend for an additional 24 months. It lists 13 lots covered by 51 suppliers, including 16 new to the framework. Two lots are named for the kind of room a mental health ward needs: Lot 3, Challenging Environment Furniture, and Lot 5, Multi-sensory. Supply route is Direct and eDirect: a quote through the NHS Supply Chain Category Team, which issues a Unique Reference Number to put on the purchase order. The brief lists suppliers for the whole agreement and does not say which supplier holds which lot, so which of the 51 are on Lot 3 or Lot 5 is not verified. Whether the extension will be taken is not verified.
localIntel.quote: Lot 3: Challenging Environment Furniture
localIntel.use: This is the national route a mental health trust can use for ward furniture built for challenging environments and for sensory rooms, with a stated end of 11 May 2027 unless extended. A rep selling into those rooms would need to be on this agreement or sell through a supplier that is; which suppliers sit on which lot has to be asked of the Facilities and Office Solutions category team, not assumed.

localIntel.org: NHS Commercial Solutions
localIntel.title: Framework Agreement for Anti-ligature, Specialist and General Doors, Windows, Furniture, Accessories and Associated Services, 13 suppliers
localIntel.fact: The Contracts Finder notice records an award dated 20/09/2023 to 13 suppliers, with a start of 27/09/2023 and an end of 26/09/2027, matching the four years the description states. The description names the lots as Lot 1 Consultancy and Professional Services, Lot 2 Anti-ligature Doors, Windows and Furniture, Lot 3 Specialist Doors, Windows and Furniture, Lot 4 General Doors, Windows and Furniture and Lot 5 Bespoke. The notice was run for NHS Commercial Solutions by the estates team at Surrey and Borders Partnership NHS Foundation Trust. The value shown on the notice is GBP 500,000,000; it is shown against every awarded supplier and is not verified as a per-supplier figure. Which supplier sits on which lot is not verified.
localIntel.quote: A Framework Agreement for Anti-ligature, Specialist and General Doors, Windows, Furniture, Accessories and Associated Services
localIntel.use: The framework a mental health estates team can call off for anti-ligature doors, windows and furniture, running to 26/09/2027, so a re-let is likely to be tendered in the year before. One of the suppliers named here, Kingsway Group, also holds a trust door call-off recorded on this desk. Whether any given trust call-off was made under this framework is not verified unless the notice says so.

localIntel.org: Hertfordshire Partnership University NHS Foundation Trust
localIntel.title: HPFT - Installation of Anti-ligature Doors for Seward Lodge, C.L.C. Contractors Limited
localIntel.fact: C.L.C. CONTRACTORS LIMITED is the named supplier on a call-off from a framework agreement awarded 17/11/2025, value GBP 146,400, running 17/11/2025 to 31/03/2026. The notice describes the scope as supply, installation, maintenance and repair of anti-ligature doors for Seward Lodge. Its additional text records the reference SBS10166; which framework that reference is, and whether the call-off was made under it, is not verified. The stated period has ended and any extension or follow-on is not verified.
localIntel.quote: Anti-Ligature Doors includes supply, installation, maintenance and repair for Seward Lodge
localIntel.use: A mental health trust bought anti-ligature doors, installed and maintained, from a contractor rather than direct from a door manufacturer, so the buying route for this kind of work is a building contractor on a framework. A supplier of doors or hardware would reach the trust through the contractor. Other HPFT work of this kind is not verified here.

localIntel.org: Kent and Medway Mental Health NHS Trust
localIntel.title: Walmer doors, Kingsway Specialist Doors and Associated Services, Kingsway Group
localIntel.fact: Kingsway Group is the named supplier on a call-off from a framework agreement awarded 11/09/2026, value GBP 216,127.20, running 11/09/2026 to 11/01/2027. The notice gives the description as the supply of anti-ligature, specialist and general doors, windows, furniture, accessories and associated services, which is the wording of the NHS Commercial Solutions framework title. The notice does not name its framework, so that the call-off sits under that framework is not verified. What Walmer is, and the number of doors, are not verified. Any extension past 11/01/2027 is not verified.
localIntel.quote: Walmer doors Kingsway Specialist Doors and Associated Services
localIntel.use: A mental health trust spent GBP 216,127.20 on doors with one supplier in a four-month window, awarded directly by call-off, so a competing door supplier has to be on the framework the trust uses. The period ends 11/01/2027.

localIntel.org: Kent and Medway Mental Health NHS Trust
localIntel.title: Estates Capital Project - Bluebell and Foxglove Anti Lig Doors and Hardware, Safehinge Primera Limited
localIntel.fact: Safehinge Primera Limited is the named supplier on a call-off award dated 04/09/2026, value GBP 107,878.16, running 04/09/2026 to 06/11/2026. The notice describes the scope as the supply of anti-ligature doors and associated hardware for the Bluebell and Foxglove sites. The period shown has ended; any follow-on is not verified. Which framework the call-off was made under is not verified, because the notice does not name one.
localIntel.quote: Supply of Anti-Ligature doors and associated hardware for the Bluebell and Foxglove sites
localIntel.use: The same trust bought anti-ligature doors from a different supplier, Safehinge Primera Limited, from the one on its Walmer doors award (Kingsway Group), so door work at this trust is split by project rather than held by one incumbent. Safehinge Primera Limited does not appear in the NHS Commercial Solutions supplier list on this desk.

updates.title: Antidepressants: new safety measures for all patients to improve communication of the risk of suicidal thoughts and behaviours and persistent sexual dysfunction
updates.summary: New safety measures are now being implemented to improve how the risks of suicidal thoughts and behaviours and persistent sexual dysfunction are communicated to patients taking antidepressant medications.

updates.title: Finasteride and Dutasteride – updated safety warnings for psychiatric side effects and sexual dysfunction
updates.summary: The MHRA has reviewed the evidence for finasteride and dutasteride and the risk of suicidal thoughts and behaviours and has recommended further measures to minimise this risk.

updates.title: Isotretinoin – changes to prescribing guidance and additional risk minimisation measures
updates.summary: The Commission on Human Medicines (CHM) has endorsed changes to the risk minimisation measures for isotretinoin, following a review of the impact of the measures implemented in 2023. We ask healthcare professionals to review these new measures and supporting materials and integrate them into their clinical practice.

updates.title: Improving Information Supplied with Gabapentinoids (Pregabalin/Gabapentin), Benzodiazepines and Z-Drugs
updates.summary: The MHRA has reviewed the warnings regarding addiction, dependence, withdrawal, and tolerance for gabapentin, pregabalin, benzodiazepines, and z-drugs. The findings (detailed in the Public Assessment Report) were that it was necessary to strengthen these warnings in the product information and on packaging to better inform healthcare professionals and patients of these known risks.

updates.title: Isotretinoin – updates to prescribing guidance and survey of services
updates.summary: The Commission on Human Medicines (CHM) has endorsed changes to isotretinoin prescribing guidance. In addition, CHM is seeking further information from dermatology services who prescribe isotretinoin to inform any future changes to current risk minimisation measures.

updates.title: Valproate (Belvo, Convulex, Depakote, Dyzantil, Epilim, Epilim Chrono or Chronosphere, Episenta, Epival, and Syonell▼): updated safety and educational materials to support patient discussion on reproductive risks
updates.summary: Updated safety and educational materials are now available to support the implementation of the regulatory measures announced in the November 2023 National Patient Safety Alert and the September 2024 Drug Safety Update. They also include previous updates to product information on the risk of low birth weight in children exposed to valproate during pregnancy.

updates.title: Valproate (Belvo, Convulex, Depakote, Dyzantil, Epilim, Epilim Chrono or  Chronosphere, Episenta, Epival, and Syonell▼): review by  two specialists is required for initiating valproate but not for  male patients already taking valproate
updates.summary: Review by two specialists remains in place for patients initiating valproate under 55 years of age but the Commission on Human Medicines (CHM) has advised that it will not be required for men (or males) currently taking valproate. Three infographics have been developed to provide clarity regarding valproate prescribing.

updates.title: Valproate use in men: as a precaution, men and their partners should use effective contraception
updates.summary: A retrospective observational study has indicated a possible association between valproate use by men around the time of conception and an increased risk of neurodevelopmental disorders in their children. Inform male patients who may father children of this possible increased risk and the recommendation to use effective contraception during valproate treatment and for at least 3 months after stopping valproate.
